The '''2005–06 season'''<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/teams/te597/fc-barcelona/all-matches/ |title=FC Barcelona » Fixtures & Results 2005/2006 |website=Worldfootball.net |date=2017-05-29 |access-date=2017-06-15 |archive-date=2017-06-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170610154508/http://www.worldfootball.net/teams/fc-barcelona/2006/3/ |url-status=live }}</ref> was '''[[FC Barcelona|Futbol Club Barcelona]]''''s 107th season in existence and 77th consecutive season in the top flight of Spanish football, [[La Liga]]. It was manager [[Frank Rijkaard]]'s third season in charge of the club, a season in which he managed to successfully retain the La Liga title, as well as winning the [[UEFA Champions League]] and [[Spanish Super Cup]]. The squad was largely unchanged from the previous season, with only two players – [[Santiago Ezquerro]] and [[Mark van Bommel]] – joining the club. [[Gerard López|Gerard]] left on a free transfer during the summer.

[[Samuel Eto'o]] was once again the top scorer for the team, improving on his tally of 29 goals from the 2004–05 season by five goals, including one in the [[2006 UEFA Champions League Final|Champions League final]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/club/historia/jugadors_de_llegenda/etoo.html |title=SAMUEL Eto'o &#124; FCBarcelona.cat |website=www.fcbarcelona.cat |access-date=26 January 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20110810191157/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/club/historia/jugadors_de_llegenda/etoo.html |archive-date=10 August 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Ronaldinho]] and Eto'o were selected in the 2005–06 [[FIFPro#Awards|FIFPro XI]] at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.worldx1.fifpro.org/index.php?mod=one&id=13281 |title=Fifpro |website=www.worldx1.fifpro.org |access-date=15 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061211065309/http://www.worldx1.fifpro.org/index.php?mod=one&id=13281 |archive-date=11 December 2006 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
